BiblicalUsage: This noun never occurs in the New Testament. Strong's lists it, but no verse uses it. The word readers actually meet is the adjective, akathartos — unclean — as in Revelation 17:4, where the woman holds a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and filthiness of her fornication. That word has its own study; this entry stands only to point you to it.
TheologicalSignificance: A word with no verse of its own carries no doctrine; its weight is the picture it points to — a golden cup full of filth, Babylon's glamour outside and corruption inside.
